r0059.title: sondern – "не X, а Y"
r0059.content_md_en:
### sondern – "not X, but Y"

sondern is used only after a negation (kein/nicht), when one statement is denied and the correct one is given instead.

Ich kaufe kein Brot, sondern Kuchen. – I am not buying bread, but cake.

### What sondern can negate
Any part of the sentence can be denied and replaced, not only a noun:
Noun: kein Brot, sondern Kuchen
Adjective: nicht schön, sondern hässlich
Adverb: nicht heute, sondern morgen
Verb/action: Er singt nicht, sondern tanzt. – He is not singing, he is dancing.

### Word order
sondern is a coordinating conjunction (like aber/und/oder), position 0, the word order after it does not change.

⚠ Do not confuse it with aber: aber is a plain "but" (a contrast without negating the first part), sondern always follows nicht/kein and replaces what was denied with the correct version.

### nicht nur …, sondern auch – "not only …, but also …"
Here sondern works the other way round: it denies nothing, it adds the second part to the first. The first one stays true.
Ich kaufe nicht nur Brot, sondern auch Kuchen. – I am buying not only bread, but also cake.
Sie spricht nicht nur Deutsch, sondern auch Englisch. – She speaks not only German, but also English.

💡 Everything depends on auch: without it a replacement, the bread is not bought; with it an addition, the bread is bought too.
r0059.noteEn:
sondern – only after a negation (kein/nicht), it replaces what is denied with the correct variant. It can deny and replace any part of speech – noun, adjective, adverb, verb, not only nouns.
In the pair nicht nur … sondern auch the meaning is the opposite – not a replacement but an addition. Other paired conjunctions are covered in r0057.

r0067.title: Условие без wenn: Sollte …, müsste …
r0067.content_md_en:
[sub] wenn is dropped — the position of the verb takes over its job
### Two forms of one condition
A wenn-clause sends the verb to the end. Remove wenn and the condition does not disappear — it is now marked by the verb itself, which has moved to first position.
Wenn keine Lösung gefunden wird, muss ich kündigen.
Sollte keine Lösung gefunden werden, müsste ich kündigen.
💡 Why this reads unambiguously: in a normal declarative sentence the first position is taken by the subject or an adverbial, and the verb stands second. A verb in first position happens in only three cases — a question without a question word, a command, and this condition. There is nothing to confuse it with.
### sollte means "if it should happen", not "must"
There is no modal obligation here. This is Konjunktiv II of sollen, and it marks the case as hypothetical.
Wenn keine Lösung gefunden wird – when there will be no solution. The speaker is almost certain of it.
Sollte keine Lösung gefunden werden – if no solution should be found. The speaker allows that it may work out.
### The consequence has to be just as hypothetical
The condition is in Konjunktiv — so the main clause has to be in Konjunktiv too. Otherwise the form breaks: a hypothesis in the first half, a fact in the second.
muss ich kündigen – I am terminating. This is an ultimatum.
müsste ich kündigen – I would have to terminate. This is a possibility with a way out.
⚠ The politeness rule in German letters is simple: the further a form stands from fact, the softer it sounds. Konjunktiv moves what is said into the area of the possible and leaves the addressee a way out.
### Why this construction uses the passive [collapse]
gefunden werden means "will be found", not "you will find". The agent is not named, and that is done on purpose.
Sollte keine Lösung gefunden werden – if no solution is found. Nobody is blamed.
Sollten Sie keine Lösung finden – if you do not find a solution. The same condition, but the finger now points at the addressee.
r0067.examplesEn:
Sollte keine Lösung gefunden werden, müsste ich den Vertrag kündigen. – If no solution is found, I would have to terminate the contract.
Sollten Sie Fragen haben, melden Sie sich gern. – Should you have any questions, feel free to get in touch.
Sollte es regnen, bleiben wir zu Hause. – If it should rain, we will stay at home.
Wenn keine Lösung gefunden wird, muss ich kündigen. – When no solution is found, I am terminating the contract.
Hätte ich mehr Zeit, würde ich helfen. – Had I more time, I would help.
r0067.noteEn:
⚠ sollte in a condition is not "must" but Konjunktiv II with the meaning "if it should happen".
The order of verbs in a subordinate clause is covered in r0029, Konjunktiv with modal verbs in r0032 and r0045.
